name: Holy Grail Skin Co.
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. Atlanta Magazine (Nov 2025 issue) calls Holy Grail Skin Co. a 'Newcomer' that launched in April (2025), after nearly two years of R&D by two co-founders, Mary Peck and Leah Matthews. It sells DTC from holygrailskinco.com, ships in the US only, and has no retail footprint. Nothing indicates a parent company or acquirer. The Tracxn results are for different companies named 'Holy Grail' or 'Holy Grail Inc.' (incorporated 2019, with Y Combinator and Accel-type investors), not this skincare brand, so they don't show any funding. The 'Best of Atlanta' award and the magazine feature are local press, not signs of scale. No priced VC round was found.
founders_supported_explanation: Leah Matthews: shown as Co-Founder of Holy Grail Skin Co. on LinkedIn, the homepage ('Leah + Mary, Co-Founders'), and the values page. Her background (Owner and Director of Studio Go since Jan 2015; Co-Founder and Director of Operations at Studio To Go since Oct 2017) matches her LinkedIn. Mary Peck: the Co-Founder role is supported only indirectly. The homepage and values pages say 'Leah + Mary, Co-Founders', and the Atlanta Magazine article names Mary Peck and Leah Matthews as the two women who launched the brand, so the first name 'Mary' reasonably maps to Mary Peck, though no cited page explicitly says 'Mary Peck, Co-Founder'. Her background is empty, so there is nothing to fail. No claim contradicts the sources, and no founder is unsupported as a founder. The label is partially_supported because Mary Peck's co-founder title is inferred from a first name plus the article's description of her as a launcher of the brand, not stated outright.

name: Stellar Beauty Co.
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. Business Wire and Beauty Independent both confirm Stellar Beauty Co. launched July 9, 2026, exclusively DTC at stellarbeautyco.com, with four products ($16-$27 in the press release). Beauty Independent says the parents (Mallory and Russell) self-funded it, so there is no VC or priced round. It was founded by a 12-year-old and is a standalone family-run brand with about 5,000 TikTok followers, so it has no national retail footprint and no parent company. The independent search results about Madison Reed, Tracxn lists of other brands, and Stellar the maintenance marketplace concern different companies and are irrelevant. One minor discrepancy: Beauty Independent says $12 to $27 while the press release lists $16 to $27, which doesn't change the verdict.
founders_supported_explanation: Every part of the claim is backed by the cited pages. Stella Dorazio is named as founder of Stellar Beauty Co. in the Business Wire release, its Yahoo Finance copy, Trend Hunter and Ypulse. The 12-year-old age and the "athlete" description are in the Business Wire release. Beauty Independent calls her an enthusiastic golfer. The class project at age 9 that led her to launch the brand appears in both Beauty Independent and Ypulse. Beauty Independent also says Stella and her mother Mallory worked together on product research, formulation and packaging. No part of the claim failed.

name: Burd Beauty
early_stage_explanation: Burd Beauty launched on Oct 22, 2025, so it is only a few months old. It sells DTC through burdbeauty.com, TikTok Shop and Instagram, with just shampoo and conditioner (plus a bundle). The press release says expansion into select retailers is still to come, so there is no national retail footprint. No funding round appears in the evidence; the Madison Reed article and the general beauty-funding articles are about other companies. The co-founder Julie Smolyansky is CEO of publicly traded Lifeway Foods, but the sources describe Burd as a new venture started by the sisters and their mother. Nothing says Lifeway owns it or that it is a subsidiary, and the site lists a personal Gmail contact. Overall it fits the early-stage criteria.
founders_supported_explanation: All three founders are shown as founders of Burd Beauty in the cited sources. The PR Newswire release and the burdbeauty.com About page say the brand was founded by Leah (17) and Misha (15) Burdeen with their mom Julie Smolyansky. Julie is called 'CEO of Lifeway Foods and co-founder of Burd Beauty' in the release, and the About page calls her a 'longtime activist for survivors of violence.' She calls herself 'a survivor and as a mom,' and the YouTube episode describes her as 'co-founding Burd Beauty with her teenage daughters.' Misha's and Leah's ages and the idea of combining their beauty-products interest into a brand that funds action come from the About page. Misha is described as co-founder in the release, and Leah is described as co-founder (the release misspells her name 'Lead'). The Trend Hunter, Instagram, and Preferred Health pages corroborate the co-founder roles and the ages. No claim goes beyond the sources, so none failed.

name: VIBES Beverages
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. The brand launched officially May 15, 2026, well inside the last 2 years, and its press releases run through Oct 2026. It is an independent LLC run by a five-person founding team, with no parent company. It has three SKUs, co-manufactured at Burma Brewing, and sells mainly through a Shopify DTC store plus kava bars. Retail is described only as 'entering key markets' or 'expanding placement', with no named national chain. LinkedIn shows just 111 followers. No funding round appears for this company: the Tracxn results (Series A/B, Accel, Fujitsu) are for a different company also called 'Vibes', a mobile marketing firm, so they don't apply. The press release's 'nationwide' and '50 states' language refers to shipping and legal compliance, not a national retail footprint. The agent's 'Pre-seed' label is a reasonable inference, since no priced round is found.
founders_supported_explanation: All three founders are shown as co-founders of Vibes Beverages in the cited sources. Jason Croxford: the press releases name him Co-Founder of Vibes Beverages (quoted as such and listed as media contact), and the claim has an empty background, so nothing else needs support. Akash Gupta: the press release calls him Co-Founder and Head of Marketing, describes him as an e-commerce growth strategist specializing in digital acquisition, SEO, backlink development and affiliate marketing, and names him Co-Founder of Total Botanical Solutions working with kratom, kava, kanna, mushroom and hemp brands. Matthew Abate: his LinkedIn lists Co-Founder at Vibes Beverages, Co-Founder at BrandOs Group, Chief Commercial Officer at Burma Brewing Company, and Co-Founder at Mitra9 Brands. It also says he co-founded and scaled Mitra9, a functional beverage company, and owned and operated a martial arts school. No claim failed.

name: Happy Panda
early_stage_explanation: The evidence supports the early-stage claim. A PR Newswire release dated Feb 2, 2026 announces Happy Panda's official market launch, so it launched very recently. The company is a DTC functional energy drink brand shipping nationwide online, with no sign of national retail distribution. The release mentions retail partner relationships, but no named national chains appear. The founders are two individuals (Cameron James and Dr. Noor A.) with no parent company. The independent results are about different entities and don't contradict this: the Tracxn Happy Panda profile is an Indian entity, and the Pitchbook, Cheeky Panda, Asset Panda and happypandawayne results are unrelated. No priced VC round or outside funding appears for this brand. Funding is unconfirmed, but nothing suggests otherwise, so the company is early stage.
founders_supported_explanation: Every claim is backed by the provided pages. The PR Newswire release (Mar 2, 2026) names Dr. Noor A. and Cameron James as founders and calls James 'co-founder and CEO'. The Yahoo Finance 'Doctor and The Athlete' release says Dr. Noor holds a Master's in Public Health and triple specialty training in Internal Medicine, General Surgery, and OB/GYN. It says 'Cam' has deep roots in professional sports and fitness plus accolades in music and high-level sales. It says the two met in the health insurance sector. It also says Dr. Noor leads B2B relationships and clinical credibility, while Cam drives direct-to-consumer strategy and lifestyle positioning. The TikTok Shop release and the About Us page tie 'Cam' to Cameron James and confirm both as founders. The westernreservenews page was not among the provided sources, but the other cited pages cover all of its claims. 'Co-founder' for Dr. Noor is accurate, though she is also described as COO.

name: Sēkwl Beverage House
early_stage_explanation: Sēkwl launched DTC on May 1, 2025 and was founded in 2025, so it is well within the last two years. No evidence of any priced VC round or outside funding. The Tracxn result is for a different company called Beverage House, so it doesn't apply. It is an independent, founder-led brand, not owned by a larger company. Footprint is small and regional: DTC plus a Colorado distributor (SMNR Sales) covering Front Range and mountain retailers. LinkedIn mentions 50+ retail locations in Colorado and across the U.S., which is modest and not national retail. The founders also bought their own production facility, but that doesn't contradict early-stage status. The agent's 'Pre-seed' label is a reasonable fit given the lack of funding evidence.
founders_supported_explanation: Every claim is backed by the cited pages. Matthew Eaton is called Founder & Chief Beverage Officer in the PR Newswire release, Yahoo Finance and BevNET. The same release calls him a beverage lover and flavor innovator. The Arvada Economic Development Association (AEDA) page describes the health scare and the turkey tail research. His LinkedIn lists Head of Responsible Sourcing at Autodesk and a senior sourcing role at VMware. AEDA names Ryan Kelley, Shannon Eurich and John Walls as cofounders. The press release identifies Kelley as Eaton's husband and Walls and Eurich as his best friends. The Our Story page labels Ryan, Shannon and John as Co-Founders (first names only) and gives the quoted descriptions: financial wizard, sales powerhouse and storytelling alchemist. The press release gives Walls the title Chief Storyteller and Head of Marketing & Communications. No claim failed.
